segments.text: Header of the kernel `read_nop256`: the loop of `asmread` with 256 `nop` instructions in each loop pass. The whole-chip test times it in part L and in control I, directly after `read_nop96` [Ref9].
segments.heading: Kernel `read_nop256`: the asmread loop plus 256 `nop`, function `k_read_nop256`

segments.text:
Start address `6cc0` (hexadecimal) and name of the function. **The loop is lines 2133 to 2399.**
- Address range: `6cd4` to `70fc`. That is 267 instructions, 1068 bytes of code. Loop start modulo 64: 20.
- Bytes read per loop pass: 256 B.
- Load instructions per loop pass: 8 (`ldp`, 32 B each).
- Other instructions per loop pass: 259 (256 `nop`, `add`, `cmp`, `b.cc`).
- The loaded values are not used.
- Source: the macro `DEF_ASMREAD` in bwx12.c, used as `DEF_ASMREAD(read_nop256, 256)` [Ref4] [Ref7].

These 5 instructions run once per call, before the loop. They are the 5 instructions of `k_asmread` (lines 61 to 65): they store `d8` to `d15` on the stack and compute the end address `x1 = x0 + 8 * n`.
The loop starts at line 2133. The 8 `ldp` instructions are the loads of `k_asmread` (lines 66 to 73): they read the 256 B that start at `x0` into `q0` to `q15`. No instruction uses the loaded values.

256 `nop` instructions: lines 2141 to 2396, addresses `6cf4` to `70f0`.
- A `nop` (no operation) changes no register and no memory.
- Source: the line `.rept 256`, `nop`, `.endr` of the macro. It tells the assembler to repeat `nop` 256 times [Ref7].
- They stand after the 8 loads and before the `add` of the pointer.
Moves the pointer forward by 256 B (`0x100` = 256).
`cmp x0, x1` compares the pointer with the end address. `b.cc 6cd4` jumps back to line 2133 while the pointer is lower (unsigned compare).
These 4 instructions run once per call, after the loop. They load `d8` to `d15` back from the stack and raise the stack pointer by 64 B.
`ret` returns to the caller. The function returns no value.
